claims.text: Two QA tutors and a tutor ask how to choose between following the requested output format and other response qualities, including factual accuracy; one QA tutor identifies a JSON-versus-prose case.

Current guidance requires scoring factual accuracy and instruction adherence separately and checking whether the requested structure was mandatory. Missing an explicit required format is a major instruction-adherence defect; a factual error is major when it changes the central conclusion or actionable answer.

Current guidance establishes no universal tie-break rule for competing accuracy and instruction-following defects. If the actual pair and applicable guidance do not settle the preference, provide the prompt and both responses for confirmation rather than inferring a general priority rule.

In the tutor's thread, the team lead requests the exact formatting instruction so QA can verify whether it was mandatory before weighing the responses. This instruction applies to that thread, not as independent project guidance.

An earlier batch's calibration follow-up recorded improved agreement in its reviewed sample but retained one disputed pair because the packet did not establish whether an output-format constraint was mandatory. That outcome did not establish a universal accuracy-versus-format preference rule.

k:response-preference-instructions@1.1:a.excerpt:
## Content-quality rubric
Major/minor describe task-quality defects and do not determine operational incident severity.

| Dimension | Major defect | Minor defect | Acceptable / no automatic penalty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Factual accuracy | Error changes the central conclusion or actionable answer | Nonessential background error without that effect | Accurate paraphrase or an immaterial stylistic difference |
| Instruction adherence | Explicit required format/structure is missing | Limited violation of an actual secondary requirement | A stylistic choice that violates no requirement |
| Citation support | Fabricated reference or materially unsupported attribution | A limited citation-detail error where the source and support remain identifiable | A valid source that supports the claim |
